confirmed: Source provenance is accurate: independently read all 18 pages of arXiv 2411.00168v1 in memory, including References on pp. 15–18; no appendix is included. The arXiv API identifies v1 as published 2024-10-31. The title and eight authors match source.title_on_document and source.authors_on_document (PDF p. 1; https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2411.00168). No local full text is listed in retrieval.json.

The CHI 2026 publisher PDF returned HTTP 403. Its Semantic Scholar abstract independently confirms 36 participants, a within-subjects advertisement-design experiment, and both client and online-volunteer evaluations; the latter are absent from arXiv v1. Thus the form correctly limits its numerical findings to the preprint rather than claiming verification of CHI full-text statistics (https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:10.1145/3772318.3791329?fields=title,authors,year,abstract,externalIds,openAccessPdf,url).

has_randomized_people_study is true: a randomly selected half designed individually first and the other half with GenAI first, then they switched conditions; experts scored their actual designs. lab_rct, within_person_order, crossover, and context_class none are appropriate. This belongs in the two-screener pipeline while remaining a small randomized experiment excluded from the core for having fewer than 50 people (pp. 2 and 6–7, Fig. 1 and Sections 3–3.3; codebook Sections 3–4).

The study reports 36 recruited participants and completion of both conditions by all participants, not two independent groups of 36. There were 110 designs initially (54 human-only, 56 GenAI-supported); five noncompliant designs were excluded, leaving 105 eligible designs (52 human-only, 53 GenAI-supported), with reported means of 1.44 and 1.47 designs per participant. These design counts must not be used as participant counts; a separate post-exclusion person denominator is not stated (p. 3, Introduction; p. 6, Sections 3 and 3.1; p. 8, Section 4).

The recorded demographics match: 94% under 30, 81% women, and 67% with prior GenAI design experience. Recruitment used professional/academic channels and a large public US university campus; the source does not establish a student-only sample (p. 6, Section 3.1).

The task and procedure match: two 25-minute sessions, one or two 1080 x 1080-pixel advertisements per session for a newly launched research-group website, approximately 90 minutes overall, and an additional $40 bonus for creators of the top three designs (p. 7, Section 3.3).

The source names ChatGPT Plus accounts and DALL-E2 for generating/modifying images and permits other tools for text correction or image clipping. Section 6 additionally calls the model GPT-4 powered by DALL-E2; these are the authors’ model descriptions (p. 6, Section 3.2; p. 7, Section 3.3; p. 14, Section 6).

Five client-organization experts blind to condition evaluated the designs. Creativity and unconventionality used 7-point ratings; usefulness used an 11-point rating (p. 4, Fig. 2; pp. 7–8, Sections 3.2–3.3).

S1-O1 reported string is numerically accurate: GenAI M = 3.909, SD = 1.389 versus human-only M = 3.457, SD = 1.359; Z = −3.318, p < .001; the prose says 13% more creative (p. 9, Section 4.1 and Fig. 3).

S1-O2 reported string is numerically accurate: GenAI M = 4.262, SD = 1.328 versus human-only M = 3.457, SD = 1.250; Z = −5.958, p < .001; the prose says 23.3% more unconventional. The Fig. 3 caption separately prints p < 0.0001 for unconventionality; the form accurately follows the Section 4.1 prose (p. 9).

S1-O3 reported string is accurate: usefulness Z = −0.238, p = .812. Figure 3 prints p-value 0.812 and plots, without labeling exact values, the arm means. The same Z and p are indeed also printed for the self-reported-design-skill analysis, so the duplication is in the source (p. 8, Sections 3.4 and 4.1; p. 9, Fig. 3).
The one-line finding faithfully reproduces the three design-outcome contrasts in arXiv v1 (pp. 8–9, Section 4.1 and Fig. 3); it does not establish that these are the final CHI numerical results.

This is an original experiment, not a synthesis; the empty synthesis fields are appropriate. No quantitative across-person homogenization/diversity outcome is reported, and no supplementary-material location is stated in the preprint (full PDF, pp. 1–18).
summary: The preprint confirms a randomized 36-person crossover study below the core sample-size threshold, and the three reported design contrasts are accurate. Corrections concern unreported analysis denominators/units, omitted outcomes and preregistration, and a nonverbatim quotation.
